_README: Hand-written corrections layered on top of applicability.json by
general_map.load_applicability(). Keys present here REPLACE the
audit's list for that ruling; keys absent fall through to the audit.
Only 'applies', 'excluded' and 'uncertain' are read -- anything else (like
this note) is ignored, so explain yourself freely.
This file is authoritative: re-running audit.py never touches it.

_why: Audit reverted to status quo on purpose -- the question is editorial, not factual.
Rule: 'You may only reroll dice when gaining food from the birdfeeder and not
when gaining food from the supply.' The predicate selects birds that gain from
the SUPPLY, i.e. exactly where the rule says reroll is NOT available.
The audit split 27 exclude / 77 keep across cards that are indistinguishable:
Common Tern ('gain 1 [fish] from the general supply') was excluded as 'no dice
are rolled', while American Goldfinch ('Gain 3 [seed] from the supply') was kept
as 'the ruling correctly warns no reroll is available'. Same facts, opposite
conclusions -- because the real question is whether a ruling saying "you cannot
do X here" earns a place on cards where X cannot arise. That is Matej's call,
not the model's, and applying it to 27 of 104 near-identical cards would be
So: excluded emptied, all 104 supply-gaining birds keep the ruling. The 5
high-confidence 'applies' (Northern Gannet et al.) genuinely roll dice, so the
audit found a real discriminator there and it is left intact.
TO RESOLVE: if the warning is wanted, delete this override's 'excluded' and
nothing changes. If it is noise, invert the predicate to select birdfeeder
gains instead and re-audit. See domain-knowledge.md open questions.
